entries.claim: The pinned Latin Mass data independently corroborate the component's substantive Latin and expose accidental editorial variants for collation.

locator.section: Common prayer tones, festal and ancient tones; the long conclusion followed by the response Amen

entries.claim: The 1961 common prayer-tone pages print a responsive Amen after the long Father-addressed ending. This corroborates the response boundary only; it is not the controlling 1962 calendar or rubric system, and the proper page does not print this response.

locator.section: RG 115 a, leaf n22; full Father-addressed conclusion, leaf n202

entries.claim: RG 115 a supplies the full Father-addressed long conclusion cued after this proper body. Page 123 supplies an accented punctuation comparator. Neither proper page prints the full expansion or a separate terminal response marker.

RG 505 and Ritus XI 1 give the Postcommunion the number, mode and order of the opening orations; RG 511 i and 513–514 distinguish spoken and sung delivery. The separate responsive Amen follows from that relationship and the common prayer-tone comparator, not a response marker on p. 55.

Printed p. 55 supplies the proper body w001–w014 and a short Per Dominum cue. The selected long Father-addressed conclusion is supplied separately from RG 115 a, p. xvii, with accented punctuation comparator p. 123; terminal Amen is a separate response, not a marker on the proper page.
